content: 1. Both raltegravir and lamivudine increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely when using these drugs. 2. Lapatinib increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 3. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 4. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the larotrectinib dose by 50%. Resume the prior dose after the CYP3A4 inhibitor has been discontinued for 3–5 half-lives. 5. Tipranavir decreases the levels or effects of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. This interaction is contraindicated. P-gp inducers reduce sofosbuvir levels, thereby decreasing the conversion to its active metabolite (GS-331007), which is responsible for 90% of its pharmacologic effect. 6. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lefamulin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of lefamulin with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 7. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid coadministration of lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 8. Lenacapavir coadministration with tipranavir/ritonavir may result in loss of therapeutic effect and development of resistance. The use of tipranavir/ritonavir with lenacapavir is not recommended. 9. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of letermovir by mechanisms involving CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Coadministration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 10. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine, potentially requiring dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 11. Levo-ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Ketoconazole doses should not exceed 200 mg/day when used concurrently. 12. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of levomilnacipran by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 13. Tipranavir significantly alters estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use a nonhormonal contraceptive method as an alternative. 14. Tipranavir decreases the effects of linagliptin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Tipranavir decreases the effects of liraglutide, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Monitor closely. 16. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lofepramine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lofexidine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Concomitant use with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may increase lofexidine plasma levels. Monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia, and consider dose reduction. 18. Tipranavir increases lomitapide levels several-fold by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 19. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 20. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 22. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3 plasma half-lives. 23. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the increased risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 24. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to 1 tablet daily for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. 25. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. Coadministration of lurasidone with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 26. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 27. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure caused by systolic dysfunction. 28. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 29. Tipranavir decreases the effects of miglitol, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Monitor closely. 30. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of mipomersen, and both drugs have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely.
